Avalanche method: minimums on every debt, extra money attacks the highest APR first.

📖 How to use

  1. Add one row per debt with its name, balance, APR and minimum payment (up to 8).
  2. Enter any extra amount you can pay each month.
  3. Read your payoff order, months to debt-free and total interest.
  4. Check the per-debt table to see when each individual debt clears.

❓ Frequently asked questions

What is the avalanche method?

The avalanche method pays minimums on every debt, then puts any extra money toward the highest-APR debt first. Mathematically it minimizes total interest, though the snowball method (smallest balance first) can feel more motivating.

What assumptions does the simulation make?

The plan assumes fixed minimum payments and APRs, on-time payments, and no new borrowing or fees. If a debt's minimum does not even cover its monthly interest, the tool tells you instead of simulating forever.

Does this affect my credit or share my debts?

No — this is a planning estimate for your eyes only. Nothing is sent anywhere; it runs entirely in your browser.
